contract_topic: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, and the Power Iteration

learning_request.learning_goal: Understand and apply power iteration, interpret the quality of an approximate eigenpair, and recognise the principal assumptions and limitations that affect convergence.

target_capabilities.description: Explain the purpose of power iteration and carry out or trace its matrix-vector multiplication and normalisation update.
Use an eigenvalue estimate and residual to interpret the quality of an approximate eigenpair and a stopping decision.
Recognise and explain the main assumptions, failure conditions, or limitations relevant to a selected power-iteration pathway.
Read, trace, or construct an executable implementation of power iteration with basic input, breakdown, and stopping safeguards.

learner_profile.authentic_context_boundary: Use ranking or spectral-computation examples only with their assumptions stated; do not equate simplified power iteration with a production ranking system.

learning_units.purpose: Eigenpairs and the motivation for iteration

contract_items.canonical_statement: For A in R^{n x n}, a non-zero vector v is an eigenvector when Av=lambda v; lambda is its associated eigenvalue. The non-zero condition is essential.
conditions: A is a real n by n matrix.
v is non-zero.
prohibited_drift: Do not allow the zero vector as an eigenvector carrying eigenvalue information.
Do not interchange the roles of v and lambda.

contract_items.canonical_statement: Eigenvalues are roots of det(A-lambda I)=0; for large matrices, iterative matrix-vector products are presented as a preferable numerical strategy to explicitly forming the characteristic polynomial.
conditions: I is the identity matrix of compatible dimension.
prohibited_drift: Do not replace the characteristic equation with a different determinant convention without review.
Do not present the iterative-strategy statement as an exact algebraic equivalence.

contract_items.canonical_statement: For a real symmetric matrix A=A^T, the spectral theorem supplies an orthonormal basis of real eigenvectors, giving A=Q Lambda Q^T and representing every x as a sum of eigenvector components with c_i=v_i^T x.
conditions: A is real and symmetric.
Q has eigenvectors as columns and is orthogonal.
prohibited_drift: Do not claim this orthogonal real decomposition for arbitrary non-symmetric matrices.
Preserve the coefficient relation c_i=v_i^T x.

contract_items.canonical_statement: The eigenvalues are ordered by magnitude as |lambda_1|>|lambda_2|>=...>=|lambda_n|, so lambda_1 is unique in magnitude and is the dominant eigenvalue.
conditions: The strict first inequality is required for a unique dominant magnitude.
prohibited_drift: Do not replace largest magnitude with largest algebraic value.
Do not weaken the strict dominant-gap condition when stating the convergence result.

contract_items.canonical_statement: Starting from a non-zero x_0, power iteration computes y_{k+1}=Ax_k and normalises x_{k+1}=y_{k+1}/||y_{k+1}||_2; normalisation controls scale without changing direction.
conditions: x_0 is non-zero.
The normalising denominator is non-zero.
prohibited_drift: Do not omit normalisation from the displayed update rule.
Do not describe normalisation as changing the iterate direction.

contract_items.canonical_statement: Under the symmetric eigenbasis expansion, A^k x_0 separates the dominant term lambda_1^k c_1 v_1 from terms scaled by (lambda_i/lambda_1)^k; a non-zero c_1 and a strict magnitude gap make the subordinate ratios vanish.
conditions: A is in the real symmetric setting with the stated eigenbasis.
c_1=v_1^T x_0 is non-zero.
|lambda_1|>|lambda_2|.
prohibited_drift: Do not drop the initial projection condition.
Do not claim all components vanish without the magnitude comparison.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Present the spectral expansion and dominant-component conclusion using the repeated-matrix-product update as application context, without requiring the normalised update as a mathematical prerequisite.

contract_items.canonical_statement: For a real symmetric matrix, a unique dominant magnitude, non-zero initial projection onto v_1, and no zero Ax_k iterate imply that direction error generally decreases asymptotically at a rate governed by |lambda_2/lambda_1|^k.
conditions: A is real and symmetric.
|lambda_1|>|lambda_2|.
The initial vector has non-zero projection onto v_1.
No iterate produces Ax_k=0.
prohibited_drift: Do not state convergence without all three listed assumptions.
Do not turn the generally asymptotic rate into an unconditional finite-iteration error bound.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: State the real-symmetric hypotheses, non-zero dominant projection, no-breakdown condition, and asymptotic rate without presenting the full eigenbasis derivation.

contract_items.canonical_statement: When lambda_1<0, successive normalised iterates may alternate sign; this is not failure because v_1 and -v_1 describe the same eigendirection.
conditions: The dominant eigenvalue is negative.
prohibited_drift: Do not interpret sign alternation alone as failure to converge in direction.
Do not identify v_1 and -v_1 as different eigendirections.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Explain sign equivalence of eigenvectors locally without the broader largest-magnitude comparison.

contract_items.canonical_statement: The Rayleigh quotient rho(x_k)=x_k^T A x_k/(x_k^T x_k), reducing to x_k^T A x_k for a normalised vector, estimates lambda_1 as x_k approaches v_1 for symmetric A.
conditions: x_k is non-zero for the quotient.
The convergence-to-lambda_1 statement uses a symmetric matrix and x_k approaching v_1.
prohibited_drift: Do not use the simplified quotient for an unnormalised vector without its denominator.
Do not claim the quotient targets the dominant eigenvalue under conditions not stated in the source.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Define the Rayleigh quotient for any non-zero vector before connecting it to power-iteration iterates.

contract_items.canonical_statement: The eigenpair residual is r_k=Ax_k-rho(x_k)x_k; an exact eigenpair has zero residual, and ||r_k||_2 is a meaningful computational stopping measure because vector differences can be distorted by sign flips.
conditions: rho(x_k) is the Rayleigh quotient used with x_k.
prohibited_drift: Do not replace the residual test with only successive-vector similarity.
Do not omit the sign ambiguity when interpreting vector differences.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Define the residual and its zero-eigenpair property without comparing residual stopping with sign-sensitive iterate differences.

contract_items.canonical_statement: The stated algorithm normalises x_0, applies matrix-vector multiplication and normalisation, checks breakdown, computes the Rayleigh estimate and residual, stops when the residual norm is at most epsilon, and otherwise stops after K iterations.
conditions: x_0 is non-zero.
epsilon is positive.
K is the maximum iteration count.
prohibited_drift: Do not move the breakdown check after division by ||y||_2.
Do not remove either the residual tolerance stop or the maximum-iteration fallback.

contract_items.canonical_statement: If v_1^T x_0=0, the initial vector has no dominant eigendirection component, exact arithmetic cannot create it, and power iteration will not converge to v_1.
conditions: The dominant eigenvector is v_1 and the initial projection is exactly zero.
prohibited_drift: Do not imply that repeated multiplication creates a missing exact eigencomponent.
Do not treat this case as ordinary slow convergence to v_1.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Use the eigenbasis coefficient statement to explain the missing projection without reproducing the complete convergence expansion.

contract_items.canonical_statement: If the two largest eigenvalue magnitudes are equal, a unique eigenvector need not be selected; if their ratio is close to one while still separated, convergence can be very slow.
conditions: The equal-magnitude case has |lambda_1|=|lambda_2|.
The slow-convergence case has |lambda_2/lambda_1| close to one.
prohibited_drift: Do not conflate non-unique dominance with merely slow convergence.
Do not promise a unique eigenvector when the dominant magnitude is repeated.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Explain tied dominant magnitude and slow convergence using the magnitude ratio without presenting the full component derivation.

contract_items.canonical_statement: Power iteration targets the eigenvalue of largest magnitude, not necessarily the most positive eigenvalue; between 5 and -8, -8 is dominant by magnitude.
conditions: Eigenvalues are compared by absolute value.
prohibited_drift: Do not describe the target as the largest algebraic eigenvalue.
Preserve the negative example's conclusion.

contract_items.canonical_statement: Although power iteration applies to some non-symmetric matrices, the clean orthogonal decomposition is not generally available; defective matrices, complex dominant eigenvalues, and non-normal behaviour require additional care and are outside these notes' scope.
conditions: The core convergence explanation is restricted to the real symmetric setting.
prohibited_drift: Do not generalise the symmetric proof or convergence claim to all non-symmetric matrices.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: State that the clean orthogonal real decomposition and bounded convergence explanation are restricted to the symmetric setting, without teaching the full symmetric proof.

contract_items.canonical_statement: The Python implementation converts A and x0 to floating NumPy arrays, requires A to be square and x0 to have compatible one-dimensional shape, rejects a zero initial vector, and normalises x before iteration.
conditions: NumPy is available.
A and x0 can be converted to floating arrays.
prohibited_drift: Do not remove the square-matrix, dimension, or non-zero-initial-vector checks.
Do not silently change the stated exception behaviour.

contract_items.canonical_statement: Each Python iteration computes y=A@x, raises RuntimeError when A@x is zero, normalises x, computes the Rayleigh estimate and residual norm, returns early when residual_norm<=tolerance, and otherwise returns the final values at max_iterations.
conditions: The iteration range is 1 through max_iterations inclusive.
The returned tuple is (eigenvalue, x, residual_norm, iteration count).
prohibited_drift: Do not divide by a zero y norm before raising the breakdown error.
Do not change the residual-based early return or the four-value return structure.

contract_items.canonical_statement: For A=[[4,1],[1,2]] with x0=(1,1), the exact eigenvalues are 3+sqrt(2) and 3-sqrt(2); the implementation should estimate the dominant value 3+sqrt(2) and produce a small residual.
conditions: The implementation is run with the supplied initial vector and default parameters.
prohibited_drift: Do not identify 3-sqrt(2) as the dominant eigenvalue for this matrix.
Do not treat a small residual as requiring a particular sign of the eigenvector.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Supply the exact eigenvalues as given, identify the example-specific dominant eigenvalue by a short local magnitude comparison, and check the dominant estimate and residual without deriving the characteristic polynomial or revisiting the general magnitude distinction.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Matrix-vector products
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Interpret and compute A x for a real square matrix and a compatible vector; exclude matrix multiplication theory beyond what the Contract items use.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: Eigenpair equations and every power update require matrix-vector multiplication.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Euclidean vector norms and normalization
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Define the Euclidean norm, normalize a non-zero vector, and recognize zero-vector breakdown; exclude general normed-space theory.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: Normalization and residual norms are operational requirements of the selected algorithm and implementation.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Orthogonality, orthonormal bases, and projection coefficients
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Use inner products to explain orthogonality, orthonormal bases, and scalar projection coefficients v_i^T x; exclude the spectral theorem and eigenbasis expansion because those belong to RC-003 and RC-006.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: The convergence condition needs minimal projection knowledge, while the spectral expansion and missing-projection failure depend on the Contract's orthogonal coordinates.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Determinants and characteristic polynomials
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Interpret det(A-lambda I)=0 for small matrices; exclude symbolic algorithms for large characteristic polynomials.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: Within RC-002, determinants and characteristic polynomials are required to understand the characteristic-equation route when that item is selected; pathway-level optionality must not weaken this item-level prerequisite.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Inner products and quadratic forms
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Compute x^T A x, x^T x, and compatible scalar-vector expressions used by the Rayleigh quotient and residual; exclude general quadratic-form classification.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: The Rayleigh quotient and its use in the residual require these operations.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Basic NumPy vector operations
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Use array conversion, shape inspection, matrix-vector multiplication, norms, comparisons, exceptions, and tuple returns needed by the Contract implementation; exclude unrelated NumPy APIs.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: The implementation and worked runtime result require reading or writing the specified NumPy routine.
